notes.title: Patch Notes v1.4.9
notes.content:
[h1]Patch Notes v1.4.9[/h1]

[b]I hate Fonts[/b]
For the benefit of you few kindly souls who read my patch notes, I'm going to break with tradition and explain [i]why[/i] this patch exists before I go on to explain what purpose it serves. 

Back in 2015 when work on the game began, it seemed a cool and fun idea to create the entire user-interface using pure fixed-width text characters - as if the user-interface were a pre-GUI retro-console display screen overlay.

For example, these characters:

┏━━━━━┓
┃━━━━━┃
┗━━━━━┛

in-game are used to draw the EMU:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40406344/090199187587d3565890b00fb5add2c21a030b72.png[/img]

And the background isn't a black image.... it uses one or more of this character: █

So the UI in Ctrl Alt Ego is essentially a text buffer if you know what one of those is, with weird characters and rich-text markup to tweak colors and sizes.

It's been absolute hell to work with. Don't ever do it.

I have implemented so much weird mathematics to get the UI to lay itself out and resize correctly. It's been 9 years of pain. Localization added a whole new layer of pain on top... because now all my weird mathematics has to account for different fonts.

I'm saying weird mathematics, because I never really understood why i was having to synchronize background characters with the foreground drawing glyphs. They're all using the same font, I thought. The font is monospace fixedwidth, right? Why are there any calculations to do? Just render a background character in one layer, then render the drawing glpyh over the top of it and they should line up just fine, surely?

I have gone 9 years not really understanding why. 9 years! Mostly because I was too lazy (or too busy if I'm being more generous to myself) to drill down and try to understand what was going on.

Well a week or two ago, the publisher dev team working on the console ports discovered that the user-interface was rendering very strangely indeed in their console builds. Some characters were aligned very badly, and some characters were.... missing!

And, they informed me, and this is the punchline really, [b]the characters I'm using to draw the user-interface aren't even defined in the font![/b]

So what has been happening all this time - and that includes 2 years of the game being out there - is Unity (the game engine) has been quietly detecting the characters are missing and choosing a fallback font on the target system to use instead. That includes both on my development PCs and on player's PCs -  I mean who knows what some players have been seeing all this time if their system isn't a fairly standard Windows platform.

And so that brings me to this patch. Basically I have gone through all the user-interface code to ensure it is using well-defined font characters. Can't have the game relying on chance to render the UI properly! This has meant having to change the look of the UI slightly in some cases (hopefully not very noticeably different though).

[b]List of other Changes in this Patch[/b]
[list]
[*] GameController LeftStick can now be used to navigate menus
[*] Language Selector UX improved
[*] Yet another font related technical fix - to spread the cost of rendering too many textures all at once on level load 
[*] I've reduced the default GLOOM level for new players, been getting several complaints about game being too dark
[/list]


Patch Size: 41 MB

notes.title: Performance Overhaul, Revamped Aesthetic
notes.content:
[h1]Major Update 1.3: Performance Boost & Revamped Aesthetic[/h1]

[h2] Post-Processing [/h2]
Locations now have a simulated measure of GLOOM and HEAT, both of which impact location look and feel. Darker darks, less flat looking generally, greater lighting clarity. 

Here's a 20 second video showing some selected before and after shots:

notes.title: SANDBOX MODE has arrived: Generate your own immersive sim!
notes.content:
[h1]Game Update 1.2: SANDBOX MODE and two new missions[/h1]

[h2]Save yourself some reading, watch this 3 minute video:[/h2]

https://youtu.be/QlaUc-KjYFQ

[h2]Alternatively, read this:[/h2]

A quick tour of the 1.2 update:

Firstly, there's a new standalone mission, entitled: [b]Four Big Fat Crates[/b]. It's a self-contained puzzle. Involving four big fat crates. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40406344/ed8bd0627203f60123c7a23546b1346ae6b4f1dc.png[/img]
If you don't like puzzles, skip it. If you do like puzzles, you'll enjoy this one.

Secondly... there's another standalone mission: [b]The Tower[/b]. You start at the bottom and you've got to get to the top. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40406344/1bf4af22fb04d019ecb9acc99b51dd7ae67b6b37.png[/img]
Pretty fun diversion, many different ways to do it. There's a new half-hidden Steam achievement to be achieved in The Tower too.

The Tower was generated from... the new [b]SANDBOX mode[/b].

Enter SANDBOX MODE from the New Game screen
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40406344/213cb33e2c300ff7411f76f63cfb24b22f1719f0.png[/img]

Then look at all those settings you can mess around with. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40406344/0fef880240c1b3889f1a87196793ca8e41102615.png[/img]

Hit GO to generate your sandbox. 
If your generated level is too easy or too hard or just not to your liking, you can head back to the settings and tweak them, then hit GO and you're off again.

Once you've generated a level that you find an intriguing challenge, you can share it with friends by getting its share code (it gets copied to the clipboard) and then paste the code into your favourite Discord channel or Steam forum or Twitter or whatever.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40406344/c229848e2fd7a4782b7baa151ce072dbd5f82660.png[/img]

Then others can grab that code an USE CODE to load up the exact same settings you have kindly curated for them. 

If you come up with a seems-impossible-but-actually-it's-possible level, share it with us! Maybe we'll run a daily or weekly challenge as a way to share your creations with others.

That's about it - hope you enjoy the new stuff!

[*] Turns out the motion physics has been jittery for players with high framerates, oups. No wonder some have been complaining about over-janky / disorientating camera motion. So... in this patch I'm putting that right.

[olist]
[*] Corrected the way the physics rate and frame rate synchronise
[*] Put in a TEMPORARY (hope!) frame rate cap to give me some breathing room to do some proper fixing and testing of the physics for higher spec rigs. mainly to ensure new players don't get a horrible first impression of the game. But the game should be a lot smoother now for all players, I figured that was the biggest priority in the short-term.
[*] Enabled 'interpolation' on all physics objects. This will mean players with higher-spec PCs will get smoother looking physics. Physics 'interpolation' used to be on only 'active' objects (e.g. your current bot, or the thing you've just grabbed), but after a fair bit of testing I'm not noticing any performance benefit to that kind of optimisation. Will see how this goes, might make it a toggle option via Menu in future patch.
[/olist]

[*] Voice of The Executor still too loud, some say, so I've softened it a bit more.

Very pleased to announce a fairly major update to the demo.

There is now a completely new pre-prologue section to the game, which we're calling a Prelude because we're running out of words for sections that come before Chapter 1.

The plan is continue to grow the number of available Missions. There's room for action missions, stealth missions, problem solving missions, challenge missions, missions at new locations etc.

notes.title: Demo Update 1.5.16
notes.content:
This update is mostly about assisting first time-players to have a smoother experience during the early parts of the game, based on having watched several players play.

Many of the measures only trigger under certain conditions, and anyway only apply if HUD assists are enabled (HUD assists are enabled by default, but can be disabled).
		
[h3]First-time player assists[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added an explicit objective to open the very first DOR, only triggers if the DOR not already opened
[*] Added several new point-of-interest markers to assist first-time players
[*] Point-of-interest offscreen indicators now blink a bit and are bigger to draw more attention
[*] Added a hint for how to boot up that CAT just outside the Bug Free Zone
[*] Made it clearer one is supposed to take Pup to Launch Ctrl (as opposed to trying to Ctrl/HOP your way there)
[*] Added hints for how to use DAD to get Pup over barricade, only triggered if player taking 'too long' to figure it out
[*] Aeronautics: Added a hint to use Rocket ability to smash through barriers
[*] Launch Ctrl Warehouse: Relocated a badly placed crate that was hiding a useful traversable ladder
[*] Added point of interest indicator for each initial WORM when player nearby so that they're less missable
[*] If player is using lift when they could just fly instead, remind them they can fly
[*] Add a reminder/hint about shooting crates
[*] Debugger map: If player has spare disk and been disembodied by hostile AI, remind them they can install that disk
[*] Added a reminder/hint about filtering sensor types at one specific point to make solving something a bit easier, and slightly tweaked geometry for this same set piece to make sensor a little easier to see
[*] Added an eyepad saying 'there is no right/wrong way to do things', removed eyepad that discouraged you from spending ego - let players decide for themselves
[*] If detect player is using the first lift in egonomics to descend, inform there's no fall damage
[*] Bug Free Zone Pup escape: Remind/mention Pup can jump any time they bump into a small traversable obstacle
[/list]
			
[h3]Bug Upgrade Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Aeronautics upgrade is now the "top recommendation for new bugs"
[*] Aeronautics/ Rocket 'damage' rebranded to rocket 'bullet'
[*] Aeronautics: Beefed up initial height-restricted float to make it a little less rubbish (it's deliberately rubbish, but now deliberately slightly less so)
[*] Disassembler Drill: is now "highly recommended for new bugs" to try to steer hesitant players
[/list]

[h3]Gameplay changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Debugger map: Give the hidden MUM higher health
[*] Reprinting bug at bug printers now costs a small percentage of player ego if the bug is trapped inside a hostile dad - to incentivise staging a proper rescue.
The percentage fee scales with difficulty, so it will barely make any difference at regular difficulty or lower.
[*] Launch Ctrl warehouse: Added an unarmed bugtrap on reverse side of blocked exit door. Why? Because one player did something I didn't expect up there and a bugtrap could have made it even more cool.
[*] Made Pup slightly better at traversing over small obstacles
[/list]
			
[h3]Fixes / Corrections / Cosmetic Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fix: Bug 0's diskdrive light was showing despite not having an actual drive
[*] Fixed bad egomode collider on openable desk drawer
[*] Made double-sided a window that was wrongly only single-sided in the Bug Free Zone
[*] Fix objective 'ctrl CAT inside bug free zone' not triggering properly
[*] Fix objective 'drain ego engine' had wrong parent objective
[*] Fix collider and occlusion weirdness on detached fan model in egonomics arse end
[*] Fixed poor text layout for 'pup can bach' meta info
[*] Fix: Insights weren't showing while disembodied
[*] Fix: Exception was being thrown if change game difficulty while disembodied
[*] Improved / increased lighting in vents near first worm (was a bit too dark in there)
[*] Fattened collider on grating vent cover to try to avoid it glitching into floors/walls
[*] Made ego mode sensor filter wheel a little less sensitive (mouse). Same applies to bug tool selection wheel.
[*] Ego mode sensor filtering now supports 1990s numpad keyboard shortcuts
[*] More graceful pause/resume transition to/from the pause menu + hopefully fixed jarring clunk audio that sometimes happened when bringing up the pause menu
[*] Added demo feedback button to main/pause menu => opens link to feedback forum
[*] Fixette: Press Tab to open Tab => ensure sync the ControlsUI content the same frame - was happening 'late' (next frame)
[*] Fixette: Tidied up the Tab/Close Tab UI transition
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update 1.5.15
notes.content:
In response to feedback from a few players about there being too many slow transfers between hosts, (HOPs), this patch enables 'hurry-able HOPs'.  

So it's still Ctrl + Click to HOP between hosts (no change), but you can now optionally keep your 1990s left-mouse-button held down to hurry the transfer.

The hurry part becomes available only after you've installed your EMU - if you don't know what that means then you haven't played the demo yet - GO PLAY IT IMMEDIATELY!
